# Quality Control

## Read QC — NanoPlot

Run per variety on raw HiFi FASTQ/BAM input.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
NanoPlot --fastq CKH.fastq.gz --outdir CKH_nanoplot --plots dot --N50 -t <threads>
NanoPlot --bam MT1_reads.bam --outdir MT1_nanoplot -t <threads>
NanoPlot --bam MT3_reads.bam --outdir MT3_nanoplot -t <threads>
```

**What to check:** total yield, read count, mean/median quality (Q-score),
percentage of reads above Q20. HiFi data should show >99% reads above Q20 given
the circular consensus sequencing (CCS) accuracy floor.

## Index reference genome

The Heinz SL4.0 GFF3 includes `ch00`, an unplaced-scaffold bin (not one of the
12 real tomato chromosomes) and must be excluded from all analyses.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Trim FASTA to ch01–ch12 only
samtools faidx Heinz_SL4.0.fasta
samtools faidx Heinz_SL4.0.fasta \
  SL4.0ch01 SL4.0ch02 SL4.0ch03 SL4.0ch04 SL4.0ch05 SL4.0ch06 \
  SL4.0ch07 SL4.0ch08 SL4.0ch09 SL4.0ch10 SL4.0ch11 SL4.0ch12 \
  > Heinz_SL4.0_genome_ch1-12.fasta
  
samtools faidx Heinz_SL4.0_genome_ch1-12.fasta

java -jar ~/bioinfo_sware/gatk-4.6.0.0/gatk-package-4.6.0.0-local.jar LocalSequenceDictionary \
clean_heinz.fasta -O clean_heinz.dict

# Trim GFF3 to the same 12 chromosomes (whitelist, not blacklist)
awk '$1 ~ /^SL4\.0ch(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/' Heinz_SL4.0.gff3 > Heinz_SL4.0_ch1-12.gff3
```

## Primary Alignment — pbmm2

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
pbmm2 index clean_heinz.fasta clean_heinz.mmi --preset SUBREAD
```

## Mapping - pbmm2

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
pbmm2 align ./ref_genome/clean_heinz.mmi MT1.fastq.gz MT1_aln.bam --preset HIFI --sort \
--rg '@RG\tID:MT1\tSM:MT1\tPL:PACBIO' --unmapped -j 16 &
```
--preset = HIFI — correct for PacBio Revio HiFi data
--sort = good, produces sorted BAM directly
--sample = MT1 — correct for sample tagging
-j 16 = fine for thread count
.mmi = index — good, using pre-built index is faster

## Secondary Alignment — ngmlr (feeds Sniffles2 SV concordance track)

ngmlr has no dedicated HiFi/CCS preset; the CLR preset (`-x pacbio`) is used as
the closest available option.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
ngmlr -t <threads> \
  -r clean_heinz.fasta \
  -q MT1.fastq.gz \
  -x pacbio \
  -o sample.sam
```

## Index and Sorting bam file

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
samtools sort -@ <threads> -o MT1.aln.sorted.bam MT1.sam
samtools index MT1.aln.sorted.bam
```

## Once indexing done, verify no corruption
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
samtools quickcheck /data2/tomato/MT1.aln.sorted.bam
echo $?  # 0 = good, anything else = problem
```

## Coverage Profiling — mosdepth

Run after alignment to check per-chromosome depth before setting DP filters
for variant calling.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
mosdepth --threads <threads> CKH_heinz CKH.heinz.pbmm2.bam
mosdepth --threads <threads> MT1_heinz MT1.heinz.pbmm2.bam
mosdepth --threads <threads> MT3_heinz MT3.heinz.pbmm2.bam
```

Pull mean depth from `<prefix>.mosdepth.summary.txt`. A practical DP ceiling for
variant filtering is roughly **2.5× the genome-wide mean depth** per sample —
extreme per-base depth outliers (e.g., observed on chr2/chr10 against MbTMV)
typically reflect repeat-collapsed reference assembly artifacts rather than
genuine sequencing problems, and should be capped rather than trusted as-is.

# SNP / InDel Calling

Dual-caller concordance strategy: **DeepVariant** + **Clair3**, intersected via
`bcftools isec`. The concordant call set (`0002.vcf`) is authoritative for all
downstream analysis. This is run against both MbTMV and Heinz SL4.0 alignments.

## Caller 1 — DeepVariant (Singularity, batched per variety)

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#single command
nohup singularity exec --cleanenv -B /data2:/data2 deepvariant_1.6.1.sif \ /opt/deepvariant/bin/run_deepvariant \
--model_type=PACBIO \
--ref=/data2/tomato/ref_genome/MbTMV_clean.fa \
--reads=/data2/tomato/MT1_aln.bam \
--output_vcf=/data2/tomato/MT1.vcf.gz \
--output_gvcf=/data2/tomato/MT1.g.vcf.gz \
--num_shards=16

##batch command
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_DIR="/data2/tomato/ref_genome/heinz"
SIF="/home/biotech/bioinfo_sware/singularity-ce-4.1.0/deepvariant_1.6.1.sif"
REF="${BASE_DIR}/clean_heinz.fasta"
NUM_SHARDS=16
VARIETIES=("CKH" "MT1" "MT3")

for VARIETY in "${VARIETIES[@]}"; do
  singularity exec --cleanenv -B /data2:/data2 "${SIF}" \
    /opt/deepvariant/bin/run_deepvariant \
    --model_type=PACBIO \
    --ref="${REF}" \
    --reads="${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_aln_heinz.bam" \
    --output_vcf="${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_heinz.vcf.gz" \
    --output_gvcf="${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_heinz.g.vcf.gz" \
    --num_shards="${NUM_SHARDS}" \
    > "${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_deepvariant.log" 2>&1
done
```

`--model_type=PACBIO` selects the HiFi/CCS-tuned model. `.g.vcf.gz` (gVCF) is
**not** used in this per-sample concordance pipeline — it is only relevant for
joint multi-sample genotyping (e.g., via GLnexus), which this pipeline does not
currently perform.

## Caller 2 — Clair3 (Singularity, batched per variety)

```{bash, eval=FALSE}

##single command
nohup singularity exec --cleanenv -B /data2:/data2 \
-B /home/biotech/bioinfo_sware:/bioinfo_sware \ /home/biotech/bioinfo_sware/singularity-ce-4.1.0/clair3_latest.sif \
/opt/bin/run_clair3.sh \
--bam_fn=/data2/tomato/MT1_aln.bam \
--ref_fn=/data2/tomato/ref_genome/MbTMV_clean.fa \
--threads=10 \
--platform="hifi" \
--model_path=/bioinfo_sware/Clair3/models/hifi_revio \
--output=/data2/tomato/clair3_MT1 \
--include_all_ctgs \
--gvcf &

##batch command
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_DIR="/data2/tomato/ref_genome/heinz"
TMP_DIR="/data2/tomato/tmp"
SIF="/home/biotech/bioinfo_sware/singularity-ce-4.1.0/clair3_latest.sif"
MODEL_PATH="/bioinfo_sware/Clair3/models/hifi_revio"
REF="${BASE_DIR}/clean_heinz.fasta"
THREADS=10
VARIETIES=("CKH" "MT1" "MT3")

for VARIETY in "${VARIETIES[@]}"; do
  OUTDIR="${BASE_DIR}/clair3_${VARIETY}"
  mkdir -p "${OUTDIR}"
  singularity exec --cleanenv \
    -B /data2:/data2 \
    -B /home/biotech/bioinfo_sware:/bioinfo_sware \
    -B "${TMP_DIR}:/tmp" \
    --env TMPDIR=/tmp \
    "${SIF}" \
    /opt/bin/run_clair3.sh \
    --bam_fn="${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_aln_heinz.bam" \
    --ref_fn="${REF}" \
    --threads="${THREADS}" \
    --platform="hifi" \
    --model_path="${MODEL_PATH}" \
    --output="${OUTDIR}" \
    --include_all_ctgs \
    --gvcf \
    > "${BASE_DIR}/${VARIETY}_clair3.log" 2>&1
done
```

## Concordance — bcftools isec

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
bcftools isec -p CKH_isec_heinz \
  CKH_heinz.vcf.gz \
  clair3_CKH/merge_output.vcf.gz
```

| Output file | Contents |
|---|---|
| `0000.vcf` | DeepVariant-only calls |
| `0001.vcf` | Clair3-only calls |
| **`0002.vcf`** | **Concordant — DeepVariant's representation. Authoritative for downstream analysis.** |
| `0003.vcf` | Concordant — Clair3's representation (same positions as 0002, redundant for most purposes) |

## Split SNPs vs. InDels

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
java -jar ~/bioinfo_sware/gatk-4.6.0.0/gatk-package-4.6.0.0-local.jar SelectVariants \
-R ../../clean_heinz.fasta \
-V MT3_heinz_cc.vcf.gz \
--select-type-to-include SNP \
-O MT3_SNP.vcf

java -jar ~/bioinfo_sware/gatk-4.6.0.0/gatk-package-4.6.0.0-local.jar SelectVariants \
-R ../../clean_heinz.fasta \
-V MT3_heinz_cc.vcf.gz \
--select-type-to-include INDEL \
-O MT3_INDEL.vcf

##convert vcf to txt
java -jar ~/bioinfo_sware/gatk-4.6.0.0/gatk-package-4.6.0.0-local.jar VariantsToTable \
  -V MT1_filtered.vcf.gz \
  -F CHROM \
  -F POS \
  -F REF \
  -F ALT \
  -F QUAL \
  -F FILTER \
  -F TYPE \
  -F DP \
  -GF GT \
  -GF GQ \
  -GF DP \
  -O MT1_variants_table.txt

```

# Structural Variant Calling

Dual-track SV strategy: **pbmm2 + pbsv** as primary (HiFi-native, tandem-repeat
aware), **ngmlr + Sniffles2** as a secondary concordance track.

## Primary Track — pbsv (tandem-repeat aware)

### Tandem repeat annotation (once per reference)

Tandem repeats are a property of the reference sequence, not of any individual
sample — generate once per reference and reuse across all varieties.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
trf clean_heinz.fasta 2 7 7 80 10 50 500 -d -h
```

Convert TRF `.dat` output to BED (needed because `pbsv --tandem-repeats`
requires BED format; TRF coordinates are 1-based inclusive and must shift to
0-based half-open):

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
awk '
/^Sequence:/ { seq = $2; next }
/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+/ { print seq"\t"($1-1)"\t"$2 }
' clean_heinz.fasta.2.7.7.80.10.50.500.dat > clean_heinz_tandem_repeats.bed
```

### SV signature discovery + joint calling

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
##single command
pbsv discover \
  --tandem-repeats MbTMV_tandem_repeats.bed \
  sample.pbmm2.bam \
  sample.svsig.gz
  
##batch command
VARIETIES=("CKH" "MT1" "MT3")

for VARIETY in "${VARIETIES[@]}"; do
  pbsv discover \
    --tandem-repeats Heinz_ch1-12_tandem_repeats.bed \
    ${VARIETY}.heinz.pbmm2.bam \
    ${VARIETY}.svsig.gz
done

pbsv call \
  --num-threads <threads> \
  clean_heinz.fasta \
  CKH.svsig.gz MT1.svsig.gz MT3.svsig.gz \
  merged.pbsv.heinz.vcf
```

## Secondary Track — ngmlr + Sniffles2 (concordance)

See the Secondary Alignment — ngmlr section above for the ngmlr alignment step
and the legacy-samtools sort fix required for its SAM output.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
##single cmd
sniffles --input CKH.sorted.bam --snf CKH.snf \
  --reference clean_heinz.fasta --threads <threads>

##batch cmd
VARIETIES=("CKH" "MT1" "MT3")

for VARIETY in "${VARIETIES[@]}"; do
  sniffles --input ${VARIETY}.sorted.bam --snf ${VARIETY}.snf \
    --reference clean_heinz.fasta --threads <threads>
done

```

## Concordance Between the Two Tracks

SVs rarely land on identical coordinates across callers (unlike SNPs), so
intersection uses a breakpoint-distance window rather than exact position
matching:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
SURVIVOR merge vcf_list.txt 1000 2 1 1 0 30 merged_survivor.heinz.vcf
```

## Filtering

- `SUPPORT >= 3–5` supporting reads
- `SVLEN >= 50 bp` (separates from indels already captured by DeepVariant/Clair3)
- Consider tiering `PRECISE` vs. `IMPRECISE` calls separately

## Statistics
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
##get bam stats
samtools flagstat MT1_aln.bam > MT1_aln.stats

##Count only primary alignments (excludes supplementary & secondary)
samtools view -c -F 2304 MT1_aln.bam

#to list files in singularity
singularity exec deepvariant_1.6.1.sif ls /opt/deepvariant/bin/

##obtain stats from vcf file
bcftools stats MT1.vcf.gz | grep "^SN"

##calculate stats of concordance file
bcftools stats 0002.vcf.gz | grep "^SN" > stats.txt

##retrieve number of snps
bcftools stats 0001.vcf.gz | grep "number of SNPs"

##filter
bcftools filter -e 'QUAL < 30 || DP < 10' 0002.vcf.gz -O z -o MT1_cc.vcf.gz

##for viewing
# Count total variants
bcftools view -H MT1_filtered.vcf.gz | wc -l

# View only SNPs
bcftools view -v snps MT1_filtered.vcf.gz | less

# View only indels
bcftools view -v indels MT1_filtered.vcf.gz | less

# Quick stats summary
bcftools stats MT1_filtered.vcf.gz | grep "^SN"

```


## Notes on Interpretation

- **GT is authoritative over ALT** for allele determination in single-sample
  VCFs — phantom ALT alleles can arise from repeat-collapsed reference
  assembly artifacts.
- **NA in a joined sample column means "matches reference,"** not missing data.
- A high multiallelic site count in what should be a single-sample VCF likely
  indicates the file is actually a merged multi-sample VCF.
- HiFi's ~99.9% raw accuracy is mostly a *substitution*-error improvement;
  residual error remains disproportionately indel-based, especially in
  homopolymer runs. True biological coding-region indels cluster at multiples
  of 3 bp (frame-preserving); artifact indels cluster at 1–2 bp in homopolymer
  contexts — a useful QC check with no direct SNP-Ts/Tv equivalent.
